Steps.1: Review the schematic design of the hw_DAA. Check that signals FORCEON and !FORCEOFF of the RS232 transceiver has pull-ups to +3V3.
Steps.2: Connect the hw_DAA to a PC. Set up the FPGA to pull data through the RS232 signals (TX & RX).
Steps.3: Connect the hw_DAA to a DAA CS harness.
Steps.4: Connect the power supply to the DAA CS harness power input, using a DC power connector, banana cables, and crocodile clips (according to the attached diagram).
Steps.5: Switch on the power supply source.
Steps.6: Set 12V and 3A on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.7: Turn on the CH1 of the power supply source.
Steps.9: Connect on CH1 an oscilloscope probe to FORCEON signal (pin 12 of the IC26) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.10: Connect on CH2 an oscilloscope probe to !FORCEOFF signal (pin 16 of the IC26) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.11: Connect on CH3 an oscilloscope probe to DOUT signal (pin 13 of the IC26) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.12: Connect on CH4 an oscilloscope probe to DIN signal (pin 11 of the IC26) with x10 attenuation.
Steps.13: Set the vertical grid to 2 V/div on all the channels. Set the vertical offset to see all the channels on the oscilloscope screen.
Steps.14: Set the horizontal grid to ~2 us/div and center the horizontal trigger position around the center of the oscilloscope screen.
Steps.15: Ensure that the attenuation is set to x10 and BW limit OFF on all the channels.
Steps.16: Set the trigger level to ~2V, rising edge and source the CH3.
Steps.17: Click on the Single button to capture communication frames of the RS232.
Steps.18: Check that signals FORCEON and !FORCEOFF are high (3.3V)
Steps.19: Check that the value at the signal DOUT is the opposite than the signal DIN.
Steps.20: Take an oscilloscope screenshot (with and without zoom).
